div.p: [The following are the inclosures mentioned by Mr. Daggett in the above dispatch.]

Sir: I have the honor to inclose herewith a copy of a letter, dated the 19th ultimo, from the collector of customs at San Francisco, Cal., in which he states that he has been advised by the United States consul at Hong-Kong of the shipment from
that port for Honolulu, Hawaiian Islands, of several cargoes of sugar, and the consul expresses fear that such sugar may he intended for transshipment for the United States as the products of the Hawaiian Islands. The collector of customs at San Francisco is alive to the importance of preventing any such fraud, if intended, upon the revenue of the United States. I will thank you, however, to correspond with our minister at those islands, and ascertain whether at the present time the Hawaiian Government imposes a duty upon imported sugars, and, if so, at what rate; also to report the arrival of any of the cargoes of sugars referred to if they shall arrive at any ports of those islands, and whether it has been the custom since the treaty went into effect to import sugars into the Sandwich Islands for consumption there, and so release an equal portion of the products of those islands for shipment to this country.

A commission which I have appointed is shortly to proceed to San Francisco to investigate charges made during the last Congress that under the treaty with the Hawaiian Islands sugars have been imported free of duty which were not fairly covered by the terms of the treaty. It may be well, therefore, when making any report to your Department on the subject, that our minister send a copy of it direct to the collector of customs at San Francisco, for the use of such commission.
